wave: CORRECTNESS -- the non-UTF-8-content fix two generations ago only handled a SUCCESSFUL fs::read returning garbled bytes; fs::read itself FAILING (permission denial) still aborted the whole pipeline for .adl/.md/repo.toml files
wave_title: `f5a8b7e3` fixed `visit_adl_sources`/`audit_repository`/`visit_docs` so a file whose CONTENT is not valid UTF-8 is lossily decoded instead of crashing. That fix wrapped only the DECODE step (`String::from_utf8_lossy(&fs::read(path)?)`) -- the `fs::read(path)?` itself, and each function's `entry.file_type()?` call, were untouched and still propagated via `?`. A permission-denied `.adl`/`.md`/`repo.toml` file (the file exists and is a real, ordinary file -- `fs::read` simply cannot open it) therefore still aborted the entire `systemize`/`code_analyze`/`docs audit`/`check`/`parse`/`work prepare` run with zero report, exactly the gap the two immediately preceding generations (`10d1576a`, `a3b37e3`) had just closed for `adapter::source::visit_inventory`'s equivalent `fs::read_dir`/`classify_file` calls.

generation_model.G_n: a3b37e3f42 (fix(adapter): an unreadable file no longer aborts the whole source walk) -- stable generation this candidate was built and validated against
generation_model.gap_discovered_by: After closing the unreadable-directory and unreadable-file gaps in `adapter::source::visit_inventory`, checked whether the SAME granularity of fix (an unreadable FILE, not just garbled content) had actually been applied to the three sibling functions fixed for non-UTF-8 content two generations earlier. Direct inspection of `visit_adl_sources`, `visit_docs`, and `audit_repository` showed each still called `fs::read(path)?`/`entry.file_type()?` unguarded -- the `from_utf8_lossy` fix only ever executes on bytes `fs::read` already successfully returned. Falsified directly via the same non-root `ubuntu` account already used for the two preceding generations (root bypasses the permission checks this class of bug depends on): constructed a real repository with one readable and one `chmod 000` `.adl` file (permissions set after a normal `git commit`, matching the established realistic-scenario pattern), and reproduced the crash cleanly against the code exactly as it stood after `a3b37e3f42`: `atlas-systemizer: <root>: Permission denied (os error 13)`, zero stdout.

priority_classification: correctness / hostile-and-degraded-environment handling (priority 1/2) -- the sixth instance this session of the same defect class, and specifically the completion of the earlier non-UTF-8-content fix's own scope: that fix's own doc comments already claimed the discipline 'never abort every other artifact's processing because of it' for these three functions, but the claim was only true for the decode step, not the read step -- a documentation-implementation mismatch of exactly the kind this session's own standing loop instructions require closing in the same coherent change as the code fix.

design_decisions.question: For `audit_repository`'s manifest read specifically: an unreadable-but-existing repo.toml is a third distinct state from 'exists and parses' and 'file genuinely absent' -- how to report it without inventing a new field?
design_decisions.decision: Route it through the existing `missing_required_roles` list (the same list a manifest that exists but fails to PARSE already uses), with a distinguishing message (`repository_manifest_unreadable:<os error>`) rather than the plain `repository_manifest` string that specifically means 'file does not exist'. This reuses the existing vocabulary/channel rather than adding a new `RepoAudit` field for a rare case, while still keeping the two facts ('missing' vs 'exists but unreadable') distinguishable to any caller that inspects the specific strings -- verified by the new test asserting the plain `repository_manifest` string is absent (not merely that `missing_required_roles` is non-empty).

design_decisions.question: For `visit_docs`, does skipping an unreadable file after already incrementing `documents_total` risk an accounting mismatch (a doc counted as 'audited' with no corresponding `DocumentFact`)?
design_decisions.decision: Reordered: `documents_total` is now incremented only AFTER `fs::read` succeeds, not as soon as a `.md` extension is matched. This was a real, if minor, ordering bug the original non-UTF-8 fix's placement (`*documents_total += 1;` before the read) would have introduced the moment `fs::read` itself could fail -- caught and fixed as part of this same generation rather than left for a future one to rediscover.

stable_validator_law_compliance.claim: A `.adl`, `.md`, or `repo.toml` file that exists but cannot be READ (permission denial being the common real case) no longer aborts `systemize`/`code_analyze`/`docs audit`/`check`/`parse`/`work prepare`. `visit_adl_sources`/`visit_docs` skip the unreadable file (no accounting channel exists there, matching the scope already accepted for the content-decode fix) while every other file is still processed normally; `audit_repository` reports an unreadable manifest through the existing `missing_required_roles` channel, distinguishable from a genuinely-absent one.
stable_validator_law_compliance.self_written_evidence: Three new `#[cfg(unix)]` regression tests in `adapter/src/lib.rs`: `an_unreadable_adl_file_does_not_abort_reading_the_rest_of_the_declared_tree`, `an_unreadable_repo_manifest_does_not_abort_the_repository_audit`, `an_unreadable_doc_does_not_abort_auditing_the_rest_of_the_tree` -- each using a real `chmod 000` file, guarded by the same root-detection skip (duplicated from `adapter::source::tests`, matching this file's own existing per-module `scratch_root` precedent) already established in the two immediately preceding generations.
stable_validator_law_compliance.independent_evidence_channel: Real, rebuilt `atlas-systemizer` binary invoked as the non-root `ubuntu` account against three independently-constructed scratch repositories (one `chmod 000` `.adl` file, one `chmod 000` `repo.toml`): all three previously crashed identically (`exit 2`, 'Permission denied (os error 13)', zero stdout); all three now run to completion (`exit 0`) with the readable sibling files processed normally. Full workspace re-run (`cargo fmt --all --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo test --workspace`) and a fresh `systemize` run against the real Atlas-Studio repository itself confirm zero regression to any existing gate, blocker, or test.

implementation.adapter/src/lib.rs: `visit_adl_sources`: `entry.file_type()?` and `fs::read(&path)?` both changed to `let Ok(..) = ... else { continue; }`. `visit_docs`: same for `entry.file_type()?` and `fs::read(&path)?`, with `*documents_total += 1` moved to only run after a successful read. `audit_repository`: `fs::read(&repo_manifest)?` changed to a `match` whose `Err` arm reports `repository_manifest_unreadable:<error>` via the existing `missing_required_roles` list instead of propagating. New `running_as_root` test helper (duplicated from `adapter::source::tests`) and three new falsification-first regression tests.

overall_verdict: MATERIALIZED AND VERIFIED. A permission-denied (or otherwise unreadable) .adl, .md, or repo.toml file previously aborted the entire pipeline with zero report, even after the immediately-preceding-session's non-UTF-8-content fix -- because that fix only handled a successful read returning garbled bytes, never a failing read. Closed at all three remaining call sites (visit_adl_sources, visit_docs, audit_repository), completing the same defect class already closed for adapter::source::visit_inventory's directory and file cases. Verified with three falsification-first regression tests and real non-root end-to-end CLI reproduction, with zero regression to the real repository's own state or any existing test.
